characters.name: Aletha Kemp
characters.goal: harvest and prove the Ash Warden pear before the buyout completes

characters.name: Robin Vale
characters.goal: protect Aletha from legal ruin during the cooperative acquisition

characters.name: Gervais Orris
characters.goal: secure the corporate variety bounty to pay down farm mortgages

characters.name: Milo Carr
characters.goal: finalize the cooperative boundary survey without legal disputes

characters.name: Helen Fenn
characters.goal: preserve the cooperative's historical memory before dissolution

characters.name: Matthew Calder
characters.goal: audit cooperative assets and acquire proprietary crop genetics

characters.name: Beth Orris
characters.goal: complete seasonal pruning contracts before the land title transfers

premise.logline: An orchard loses a whole variety of pear overnight, and the grafter who bred it has to work out which of her neighbours did it and why.

modules.theme: the difference between owning work and having made it
modules.setting_time: the last autumn before a cooperative is bought out
modules.setting_place: a hill orchard shared by four families who no longer speak
modules.protagonist: a grafter in her sixties who bred the lost variety and never registered it
modules.protagonist_want: to prove the variety was hers before the sale closes
modules.antagonism: a neighbour with a legitimate claim and a bad motive
modules.complication: the person who destroyed the trees did it to protect her
modules.ending_shape: the truth is established and costs the person who established it

plot_shape.name: Mystery
plot_shape.central_question: What actually happened, and who is willing to say so?

phases.name: Disturbance
phases.purpose: A wrong surfaces and someone is obliged to look into it.

phases.name: Inquiry
phases.purpose: Evidence accumulates, most of it true and misread.

phases.name: Wrong turn
phases.purpose: A reading of the evidence that is coherent and wrong collapses.

phases.name: Solution
phases.purpose: The true account, assembled only from what the reader has already been shown.

phases.name: Cost
phases.purpose: What knowing costs the person who found out.

cast_roles.purpose: Carries the reader through the inquiry and pays its cost.
Has a reason to keep the true account from being assembled.
Holds one true piece and misunderstands its meaning.
The reason the question matters at all.

obligatory_moves: Every element of the true account is on the page before it is stated.
At least one true detail is shown early in a context that makes it look irrelevant.
The wrong reading is defensible on the evidence available when it is made.

events.summary: Aletha Kemp climbs up to her hillside terrace at dawn and finds all twenty Ash Warden pear trees sawed down to the graft roots.
events.dramatic_function: Disturbance phase begins; the protagonist discovers the complete physical destruction of her life's breeding work.
beats: Aletha climbs the limestone steps carrying picking baskets for the morning harvest.
She discovers the twenty Ash Warden trees clean-cut at stump level with the crowns carried away.
She realizes the felling destroys her proof of the variety before the buyout deadline.

state_changes.value: identify who destroyed the Ash Warden trees

events.summary: Robin Vale joins Aletha on the terrace to inspect the clean stumps, where Aletha notices an odor of linseed grafting wax on the cuts.
events.dramatic_function: Establish Robin's ostensible support while unobtrusively planting the physical scent signature of the cut.
beats: Robin arrives with clearing tools and helps examine the felled tree rows.
Robin directs Aletha's suspicion toward Gervais Orris and the contested terrace fence line.
Aletha kneels by the low stumps and detects a distinct smell of cold linseed grafting wax.

events.summary: Aletha confronts Gervais Orris at the cooperative weigh station before corporate agent Matthew Calder, who warns about cultivar penalties.
events.dramatic_function: Introduce the commercial buyout pressure and plant the threat of contractual penalties against uncertified varieties.
beats: Aletha storms into the weigh station and accuses Gervais of clearing the high terrace trees.
Gervais denies the accusation and argues that unregistered crops on shared soil are cooperative property.
Calder warns the room that conflicting cultivar claims will invoke harsh contractual audit penalties against growers.

events.summary: Milo Carr shows Aletha the boundary survey maps and mentions that Gervais recently filed for an unlisted buyout bonus.
events.dramatic_function: Conclude the Disturbance phase by giving the investigator an apparent motive pointing straight at Gervais.
beats: Milo unrolls the old parchment parcel maps showing the long-standing boundary line dispute with the Orris family.
Milo reveals that Gervais submitted a confidential claim requesting an advance on an unlisted corporate bonus.
Aletha concludes Gervais destroyed her trees to force the buyout through without her competing claim.

state_changes.value: prove Gervais destroyed the Ash Warden trees to secure his buyout bonus

events.summary: Aletha visits the Orris packing barn under pretense of borrowing crates and notes Gervais's chainsaw dripping blue mineral oil.
events.dramatic_function: Inquiry phase begins; plant the distinctive synthetic blue bar oil used on Gervais's saw.
beats: Aletha enters the Orris barn under the excuse of returning empty picking lugs.
Gervais orders her out of the barn, declaring he will not tolerate her baseless accusations.
Aletha spots Gervais's petrol saw on the workbench leaking bright blue synthetic bar oil onto a rag.

events.summary: Beth Orris intercepts Aletha outside the barn and admits her father ordered her to measure the Ash Warden terrace days earlier.
events.dramatic_function: Deepen the defensible wrong turn by adding corroborating witness testimony about Gervais's interest in the trees.
beats: Beth pulls Aletha beside the exterior haystacks to speak quietly.
Beth admits Gervais made her survey tree spacing and estimated yield on the terrace three days before.
Beth warns Aletha that Gervais is desperate for funds to settle farm liens before the sale closes.

events.summary: Aletha visits Helen Fenn, who recalls past boundary trades and mentions seeing a lone lantern moving to the nursery shed at midnight.
events.dramatic_function: Plant an overlooked witness detail regarding midnight movement between the terrace and the nursery.
beats: Helen explains the historical unwritten pasture exchanges between the ridge families.
Helen remarks that on the night of the felling, she saw a single lantern moving down from the terrace into the nursery shed.
Aletha mistakenly assumes the lantern belonged to Gervais fleeing through the lower path.

events.summary: Aletha and Milo search the safe and find Gervais's petition claiming the Ash Warden variety as cooperative communal property.
events.dramatic_function: Solidify the paper trail indicating Gervais's hostile takeover attempt of the variety.
beats: Milo unlocks the records cabinet to inspect recent formal filings.
Aletha finds Gervais's petition asking Calder to credit the terrace variety to cooperative collective assets.
Aletha becomes convinced Gervais intended to extinguish her personal breeding claim.

events.summary: Matthew Calder tells Aletha that Calder Holdings only pays variety bounties for viable, living genetic wood.
events.dramatic_function: Introduce the botanical rule that dead wood yields no corporate payout, raising a contradiction in the case.
beats: Calder reviews the inventory schedule across from Aletha at the weigh desk.
Calder explains that corporate bounties require live scion buds and documented parentage.
Aletha is left wondering why Gervais would fell the trees if only living wood could earn the money.

events.summary: Aletha collects stump sawdust on the terrace with Robin and discovers the cuts contain zero petroleum or blue chain oil.
events.dramatic_function: Pay off the blue oil plant and produce the first physical discrepancy in the theory against Gervais.
beats: Aletha gathers sawdust samples from the terrace stumps using a pocket lens.
She finds the fine kerf marks completely free of petroleum residue or blue bar oil.
Robin anxiously suggests she give up chemical testing and accept the trees are gone.

events.summary: Aletha confronts Beth Orris again, but Beth produces a stamped depot receipt establishing Gervais was in the valley all night.
events.dramatic_function: Inquiry concludes with Gervais's alibi intact, setting up Aletha's obstinate Wrong Turn accusation.
beats: Aletha returns to the packing yard demanding Beth state where Gervais was at midnight.
Beth produces a dated freight receipt from the valley press bearing Gervais's signature at 1:15 AM.
Aletha assumes Gervais hired a contract worker rather than accepting his innocence.

events.summary: Aletha convenes an emergency meeting at the weigh station and formally accuses Gervais of hiring saboteurs to fell the trees.
events.dramatic_function: Wrong Turn phase peaks as the investigator pushes her defensible but false hypothesis before all parties.
beats: Aletha presents the boundary dispute and Gervais's bonus filing before the board.
She formally accuses Gervais of paying a saboteur to ruin the crop out of spite.
Milo and Calder demand Gervais respond to the accusation before contracts are signed.

events.summary: Gervais erupts and reveals his debt ledger, proving he needed the Ash Warden trees alive to secure a fifty-thousand-dollar bonus.
events.dramatic_function: Collapse of the wrong turn reading: the suspect's economic survival depended on preserving the trees, not destroying them.
beats: Gervais slams his bank foreclosure notices onto the scale table.
He reveals that Calder promised him fifty thousand dollars if the living Ash Warden variety was delivered.
Gervais breaks down, lamenting that the felling of the trees completely ruins him financially.

events.summary: Calder produces the acquisition contract and reads Clause 14B, which imposes ruinous unlicensed propagation fines on breeders.
events.dramatic_function: Pay off the penalty plant and establish the real motive: someone destroyed the trees to shield the breeder from ruin.
beats: Calder displays Clause 14B of the acquisition draft.
He reads the term: any unregistered variety on cooperative land incurs a thirty-thousand-dollar retroactive nursery fine on the breeder.
Aletha realizes that whoever cut the trees acted to protect her from total financial ruin.

state_changes.value: discover who knew about Clause 14B and felled the trees to protect her

events.summary: Milo checks the weigh station log and tells Aletha that Robin Vale spent two hours reading the contract drafts before the felling.
events.dramatic_function: Pivot from the collapsed wrong turn directly toward the true concealer.
beats: Aletha asks Milo who had access to the Calder draft agreements prior to the felling.
Milo checks the sign-in register and shows that Robin signed out the contract folder on Tuesday afternoon.
Aletha realizes Robin knew the full text of Clause 14B before anyone else.

events.summary: Aletha searches the nursery shed, matching the linseed wax to Robin's bench and finding three living Ash Warden scions hidden in burlap.
events.dramatic_function: Solution phase begins; assemble the physical clues planted earlier to establish what really took place.
beats: Aletha searches Robin's workspace in the nursery shed.
She opens an unsealed tin on his bench and recognizes the exact linseed wax scent from the terrace stumps.
Beneath the floorboards, she finds Robin's Japanese pull-saw and three living scions wrapped in damp moss.

events.summary: Robin enters the shed and confesses that he felled the trees after midnight to prevent Calder from seizing the variety and fining Aletha.
events.dramatic_function: Collect the midnight lantern plant and character knowledge, laying bare the true protective motive.
beats: Robin enters the nursery shed and stops short upon seeing Aletha holding the scions and pull-saw.
Aletha confronts him with Helen's midnight lantern sighting and his contract review.
Robin confesses he cut the twenty trees to protect her from Clause 14B's fines and save the genetic wood.

events.summary: Aletha examines the severed scions and realizes Robin used her notched knife to salvage the variety while eradicating the standing grove.
events.dramatic_function: Crystallize the core theme: owning the standing grove versus having created the variety itself.
beats: Aletha checks the cut scion ends and notes the angled notches made by her own grafting knife.
Robin explains that standing trees on coop land belonged to Calder, but the severed scions belong to her alone.
Aletha recognizes that to defend her authorship, she will be forced to expose Robin's unlawful felling.

state_changes.value: establish her authorship of the Ash Warden while protecting Robin from prison

events.summary: Aletha brings her breeding journal and the scions to the weigh station, proving she made the pear while admitting Robin felled the grove.
events.dramatic_function: Cost phase begins; the truth is formally established, separating creation from ownership, but creating immediate legal liability.
beats: Aletha presents her twenty-year breeding journal to Calder, proving her sole creation of the Ash Warden pear.
Calder concedes the variety was bred by Aletha, rendering Clause 14B moot because no commercial crop stands on the land.
Gervais and Milo demand restitution, noting that Robin's destruction of cooperative timber is a prosecutable crime.

events.summary: Aletha surrenders her entire buyout dividend to indemnify the cooperative and clear Robin, walking away with nothing but her scions.
events.dramatic_function: Complete the ending shape: truth is established and exacts a severe financial cost on the investigator.
beats: Aletha signs over her forty-thousand-dollar cooperative buyout share to cover the timber damages and release Robin from charges.
Calder executes the deed transfer for the bare land, leaving Aletha with her journal and three dormant scion sticks.
Aletha and Robin step outside into the autumn twilight with no land or money, but holding the variety they made.

state_changes.value: replant the Ash Warden scions on independent soil
